back: The official style of arts from 1934: optimistic, accessible works showing the building of socialism and serving the party.
The 1920s policy of promoting local languages and officials in the non-Russian republics, reversed in the 1930s.

front: What did the 1936 family law do?
back: Banned abortion except on medical grounds, made divorce harder and gave payments to mothers of many children.

front: What was the League of the Militant Godless?
back: An atheist organisation founded in 1925 that ran propaganda against religion.

front: What happened to Shostakovich in January 1936?
back: Pravda attacked his opera Lady Macbeth of Mtsensk, warning artists to follow the party line.

front: How did Soviet literacy change between 1926 and 1939?
back: From about one half to about four-fifths, according to census figures.
The 1930s shift from radical social experiments to traditional family values, school discipline and national pride.

front: What was the 'double burden' for Soviet women?
back: Working full-time in paid jobs while doing most of the housework and childcare.

front: How far did Stalin transform society?
back: Greatly in work, education and cities; less in beliefs and family life, and with heavy control and fear.
